page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.24xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor family. It features 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. The multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests rank in the top 10 percent, alongside multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also achieve top-tier status, with read-only large block speeds reaching 481.24 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also demonstrate top-tier performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8gb.24xlarge offers high resource density and strong multi-core performance per resource unit, typical of AWS Graviton ARM-based architectures. The primary tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators, which limits its utility for heavy graphics or local-storage-dependent database setups. The server is highly effective for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, static web serving, Redis caching, and medium-to-large LLM text generation tasks.
